subject: ADR-165: the field notebook, recorded whole -- species, quadrats, captures, ethogram and session, every field driven
body: THE FIELD NOTEBOOK -- field-notebook.html, a tap-to-tally field book (tap a species to count individuals, a quadrat cell for presence, a 'more' counter for captures and recaptures, and a behaviour to build an ACTIVITY BUDGET, plus a session header of site/observer/date) -- WAS THE LOWEST-COVERED PAGE in the kit: its task tallied species to ten individuals across three species and worked the quadrats and capture counters, but five of its six value-carrying fields were never entered -- the whole ETHOGRAM pane (the scan interval and the add-a-behaviour box) and the entire SESSION HEADER. A tally book whose pages carry no site, observer or date is one whose counts can't be attributed, the one thing a field notebook exists to prevent. The existing scenario is kept verbatim (species counts, quadrat dispersion, capture/recapture counters), so its assertions hold, and the five untouched fields are driven: the scan interval set (30 s, the point-sample cadence fixed before the session starts), a new behaviour 'preen' ADDED AND TALLIED alongside forage to build a real activity budget the read confirms by name, and the session stamped with a site, an observer and today's date. The activity budget is read back and held to show the added behaviour, so the ethogram is exercised end to end rather than merely opened. field-notebook 1 -> 6 OF 6 FIELDS, 64 -> 80 confirmed and 0 refuted, and the kit 502 -> 507 of 521 (97%), 22 of 27 pages entered whole. Held: the ethogram board seeds five behaviours and the added 'preen' becomes the sixth; the session header is three plain text inputs reached by id. No page was edited -- a task-only slice, the fifteenth page driven end to end.
